entries.body:
The bridge between the Cosmos-based Secret network and Axelar network was exploited via an infinite bug that went unnoticed for a week. An attacker exploited a smart contract in order to mint a large quantity of Axelar tokens on the Secret network, which they then redeeemed for around $4.67 million.

The exploit, which occurred on June 10, went unnoticed until June 17, when a transaction failed with a message suggesting that more tokens had been bridged out of the Secret network than had been bridged in.

Secret has warned, "If you hold Axelar-bridged saXXX tokens on Secret, please be aware their backing was affected and your funds may be lost."
entries.title: Secret bridge exploited for $4.67 million a week before anyone notices

entries.body:
An attacker exploited a legacy that had been used by the Raydium Solana before it was deprecated in 2021. Though the contract was unused, there were still funds in the affected by the vulnerable contract. Using fake LP tokens, the exploiter was able to trick an old smart contract with insufficient validation into allowing them to withdraw assets.

Raydium has said it will compensate users who lost funds in the exploit.

entries.body:
Humanity Protocol, a decentralized identity project that uses palm scans to try to prove that users are human, has suffered a $36 million loss after attackers compromised a laptop belonging to an employee. After the laptop was infected with malware, the malicious code gained root access, then stole seven that were reportedly accidentally stored in a backup. Several of the keys were sufficient to satisfy requirements, which are intended to prevent private key leaks from allowing attackers to gain control over sensitive infrastructure like . With multisignature wallets, keys are supposed to be stored separately across multiple individuals and devices; however, in this case, attackers only needed to compromise one laptop to gain control over multisig-protected contracts.

With the keys, the attacker stole more than 6 million of Humanity's H token, then used other keys to upgrade a bridge and drain 141 million more tokens. With the bridge access, they also 300 million new H tokens. The attacker then quickly swapped the ill-gotten tokens for ETH, causing the H price to plummet by 80–90%.

Humanity Protocol markets itself as a competitor to Sam Altman's World (formerly Worldcoin), a decentralized identity project that aims to use iris scans to prove that users are unique humans. Humanity raised $20 million in 2025 from Pantera Capital and Jump Crypto.
entries.title: Humanity Protocol loses $36 million to employee laptop compromise

entries.body:
Remember when Austria's otherwise respectable Belvedere Museum sold 10,000 NFTs representing postage-stamp sized sections of Gustav Klimt's The Kiss for like $2,000 a pop? No? Don't worry, I've got you.

Only about a quarter of them ever sold, leaving about 7,200 of them on the digital shelves. That is, until they were stolen (or, as the museum put it, "transferred from the wallet without authorization"). If valued at their sale price the stolen NFTs would be worth €13.32 million (US$15.3 million), though it's hard to argue the thief could've ever sold them for that amount given the museum had failed to do so for several years.

The stolen NFTs were soon made even less appealing to prospective buyers when the museum un-linked the image files from the digital assets, and OpenSea blocked them from trading.
entries.title: Thief steals remaining 7,200 unsold The Kiss NFTs in digital museum heist

entries.body: Gravity Bridge, a bridge between the Cosmos and Ethereum blockchains, suffered $5.4 million in losses likely due compromised private keys. The developers of the protocol urged validators to halt while the theft was investigated, and the bridge was indeed halted shortly after. Two weeks after the hack, the Gravity Bridge interface remained unavailable.
entries.title: Gravity Bridge drained of $5.4 million

entries.body: DxSale, a project that was popular in 2021 for launching new tokens and creating <button class="define-target" id="liquidity-pool">liquidity pools</button>, suffered a $7.3 million exploit after ownership of a locker contract was transferred to a new address. Nine months later, the contract ownership was repeatedly moved between many new wallets — likely in an attempt to cover tracks — before $7.3 million was taken from old liquidity pools. The stolen assets were then swapped to BNB and routed through <button class="define-target" id="bridge">bridges</button> and <button class="define-target" id="tumbler">mixers</button> to obscure the trail.

entries.body:
A third-party Gnosis Safe smart contract called SquidRouterModule was exploited for $3.2 million. The smart contract included a set string that could be passed to identify a "safe" message; however, the string was visible in the public smart contract code and used by an attacker to impersonate Gnosis Safe users and then drain their wallets. 86 wallets had used the module, and lost a combined $3.2 million.

The name led to some confusion due to the similarly named Squid Router, which is not related. It's not clear if the users who installed the module were aware that the two projects were separate.
entries.title: SquidRouterModule, unrelated to Squid Router, exploited for $3.2 million

entries.body: Crypto sleuth zachxbt identified that "A Polymarket admin address appears to have been compromised on Polygon", writing that $520,000 had been drained as of the time of his post. The theft ultimately amounted to around $700,000, and Polymarket confirmed that a "wallet used for internal top-up operations" had been compromised. They did not provide further details as to how the compromise happened, though the company's VP of Engineering later said that the private key was six years old and that all private keys would be replaced with a managed key going forward.
entries.title: Polymarket loses $700,000 to private key compromise

entries.body:
The RetoSwap decentralized exchange for trading the Monero was exploited after an attacker exploited a vulnerability in the Haveno Monero exchange protocol used by the project. Users lost an estimated $2.7 million when their transactions were routed to the attacker's wallet.

Because Monero is a privacycoin, a type of cryptocurrency that obscures transaction details including sender and receiver wallets, it is not feasible to trace the stolen assets.
entries.title: RetoSwap users lose $2.7 million to Haveno vulnerability

entries.body:
An attacker stole $11.6 million in various crypto assets from the Verus–Ethereum , which allows users to use tokens from the Verus network on the Ethereum chain and vice versa. The attacker then swapped the tokens for ETH, limiting the ability for issuers of more centralized tokens to freeze the stolen assets.

Verus halted the entire Verus network after the exploit was detected in hopes of limiting further damage.

The exploiter later accepted a offer by Verus, returning 4,052 ETH (~$8.5 million) while keeping the remaining ~25% as a "bounty".
